status: Rules fixed before this benchmark run, after earlier descriptive outcomes were inspected. Exploratory retrospective pseudo-out-of-sample, not an untouched holdout.
scope: One empirical revision-interval algorithm at the six-month snapshot only. No additional fitted models, training-window alternatives, tuning or test-family searches.
outcome: Published annual count selected at the 18-month cutoff, not true migration.
primary_flow: Net migration; arrivals and departures use the identical rule as component diagnostics.
training: Country-specific expanding archive at age six; train only where mature_on is strictly before the actual early-snapshot publication date and historical endpoint precedes the test endpoint. All age-specific eligible history is admitted, including endpoints before 2019.
warmup_interpretation: Three nominal years of monthly or quarterly endpoints, not equal independent information or tail-precision guarantees. Australia actually has more history at its first test.
signed_training_revision: r_i = (Y_i,18 - Y_i,6) / (A_i,6 + D_i,6). Denominator is the early observed gross count; no future gross count enters prediction.
quantiles: numpy method='linear' (type 7); country and flow separately; no centering, truncation, zero anchoring or combination with official standard errors.
baseline: NZ published annual model interval Y_t,6 +/- 1.96 * annual published SE, on exactly the same cases. Australia has no official interval comparator in these inputs.
test: Previously planned endpoints 2019 through 2025Q1, subject to warmup. Report native monthly NZ and quarterly Australia separately; also shared quarter-end endpoints.
metrics: Coverage, directional misses, mean width and 95% interval score in migration counts; paired NZ score/width/coverage differences. Score = width + 40*shortfall below lower or above upper. Also normalize widths/scores by the observable early gross count, multiplying by 100; do not pool countries or flows.
stability: Descriptive endpoint-year and previously defined endpoint-phase summaries from the same predictions. Shared quarter-end sample is a cadence diagnostic. No significance claims or independence assumption.
limitations: Few independent episodes, overlapping annual windows, changing revision processes, sparse empirical tails. Published model intervals target a narrower uncertainty concept, so this tests usefulness for later published revisions, not calibration for their original estimand.
success_rule: Greater coverage alone is insufficient: report the width cost and whether paired mean interval score improves, including failures by flow and year. No rule changes in response to outcomes.
